title: PostgreSQL Transaction Isolation: Write Skew and Serializable Snapshot Isolation (SSI)
realWorldScenario: In a loan management system, two loan officers simultaneously approve disbursements for the same applicant under `REPEATABLE READ`. The business rule states: "Total active disbursed debt for an applicant cannot exceed $100,000." Both officers see $60,000 active debt and both disburse $30,000. Total debt is now $120,000.
questionStatement: Explain why `REPEATABLE READ` allows this Write Skew anomaly while preventing dirty reads and non-repeatable reads. Explain how PostgreSQL implements Serializable Snapshot Isolation (SSI) using SIREAD locks to detect rw-antidependencies and abort conflicting transactions with code `40001 serialization_failure`.
expectedConcepts: Write Skew anomaly definition on overlapping disjoint rows
Why Repeatable Read only protects against single-row concurrent updates
SSI (Serializable Snapshot Isolation) and non-blocking SIREAD locks
rw-antidependency tracking and dependency cycle detection
hints: Remember that two concurrent inserts create new primary keys, so they do not lock each other.
SIREAD locks are not traditional heavy locks; they do not block execution.
What must application code do when a 40001 error occurs?
